newsitem.title: USA: US, EU to complete trade pacts next month-Clinton.
newsitem.headline: US, EU to complete trade pacts next month-Clinton.

text.p: The United States and the European Union should put the finishing touches next month on a series of agreements that would knock down barriers on $40 billion worth of trade, President Clinton said on Monday.

Under the planned mutual recognition agreements, the two sides will agree to recognize the results of each other's testing, inspection and other procedures on a variety of products -- from telecommunications to medical equipment.

"This will remove barriers on $40 billion of trade between the United States and the European Union, cutting red tape for our businesses and prices for our consumers," Clinton told a news conference. "One standard, one test, one time."

The White House said in a fact sheet that the two sides had agreed in principle to wrap up negotiations on the agreements by the end of next month. The areas expected to be covered are: telecommunications terminal equipment and information technolgy equipment; pharmaceutical good manufacturing practices; medical devices; electromagnetic compatibility; electrical safety; and recreational craft.
